This application uses a standalone copy of the libheif-js 1.23.5 WebAssembly
bundle for HEIC and HEIF decoding. The package includes libheif 1.23.5 and
libde265 1.0.15. The libraries and their use are covered by the GNU Lesser
General Public License. See LICENSE.libheif-js, LICENSE, and the libde265
COPYING file linked below for license texts.

The distributed libheif-bundle.js is package/libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.js
from https://registry.npmjs.org/libheif-js/-/libheif-js-1.23.5.tgz

Corresponding source and build scripts:

* libheif-js (Kiril Vatev), npm release commit, including scripts/install.js:
  https://github.com/catdad-experiments/libheif-js/archive/d8ec4bc3bc5bf8055975577bccbbc7e1d7313c2d.tar.gz
* Emscripten release build, including its workflow and dist-prep.sh:
  https://github.com/catdad-experiments/libheif-emscripten/archive/refs/tags/v1.23.5.tar.gz
* libheif (Dirk Farin and contributors), the exact submodule revision used
  for that release, including build-emscripten.sh:
  https://github.com/strukturag/libheif/archive/413e2a87e6a70b3eccc3a3adc5801179dd2d9e00.tar.gz
* libde265 (struktur AG and contributors), the version used by that build:
  https://github.com/strukturag/libde265/releases/download/v1.0.15/libde265-1.0.15.tar.gz
  License: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/strukturag/libde265/v1.0.15/COPYING

The Emscripten workflow uses Emscripten 3.1.61. Its source tarball excludes
the libheif submodule. Use the libheif source above in the libheif directory
when building from the tarballs, or check out the Emscripten release with
its submodule. Use the workflow to produce libheif.tar.gz, then pass its
path to scripts/install.js in the libheif-js checkout after installing
the npm build dependencies. The output is libheif-wasm/libheif-bundle.js.

In a local copy of the website, replace vendor/libheif/libheif-bundle.js
with your interface-compatible build. The application loads this script
on demand and expects a browser global named libheif. You may modify
the library and reverse engineer to debug those modifications under the
terms of the LGPL.
